html:
Ukraine is a large country of black earth steppe and forest north of the Black Sea, with Kyiv as its capital. Kyiv was the centre of Kievan Rus', the medieval state that Ukrainians, Russians and Belarusians all trace back to. Later the land was split between Poland-Lithuania, the Cossacks and Russia.

On the map it appears in 1920, during a short and failed bid for independence after the Russian Revolution. It then became the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, a founding member of the Soviet Union. Stalin's forced collectivisation caused the Holodomor, the famine of 1932 and 1933 that killed millions of Ukrainians. The Second World War and the Holocaust devastated it again, and in 1986 the Chernobyl disaster happened on its soil.

Ukraine voted for independence in 1991 as the Soviet Union broke up, and it appears again from 1994. Protests in 2004 and 2014 pushed it toward Europe. Russia then seized Crimea and backed a war in the east, and in 2022 launched a full invasion.
